subject: Generation heartbeat oscillation — us-west p95 spikes (Elmwood)
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.inference>
To: Sarah Jenner <sarah.jenner@elmwoodhealth.com>
Cc: ops+elmwood@elmwoodhealth.com, marissa.cole@redwood.inference, sean.gallagher@redwood.inference
Date: 2028-03-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Generation heartbeat oscillation — us-west p95 spikes (Elmwood)

Hi Sarah —

Wanted to let you know we observed a recurring generation "heartbeat" oscillation impacting p95 latency for streamed and batched requests in us-west between ~08:50–09:05 PDT this morning. You may have seen intermittent stalls/extra-long tails in responses and a few truncated streams.

Quick summary:
- Impact: Elevated p95 (~3× baseline) for text-generation endpoints; ~1–2% increased truncation for streaming sessions.
- Scope: Elmwood production tokens routed to us-west; not affecting eu or apac regions.
- Mitigation in progress: We disabled an experimental kernel selection heuristic on the affected pool and enabled an immediate fallback policy to a near-equivalent model variant to reduce tail latency. We also initiated a rolling restart of the worker shard that showed increased kernel contention.

What we need from you: any examples of truncated or malformed responses (timestamps helpful). If you can share a single request id or two we'll correlate traces.

We've posted a short status note here: https://status.redwood.inference/incidents/USW-2028-03-01-heartbeat (will update as we learn more). Attachment: p95_heartbeat_chart_us-west.png (png) — small chart showing p95 spike window.

I'll follow up with a post-incident summary and an ETA for the full postmortem. Apologies for the disruption — we'll keep you updated as we get more telemetry.

— Olga
Olga Petrov
Account Lead, Customer Operations
Redwood Inference
(attachment: p95_heartbeat_chart_us-west.png image/png)

From: Sarah Jenner <sarah.jenner@elmwoodhealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.inference>
Cc: ops+elmwood@elmwoodhealth.com
Date: 2028-03-01T09:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Generation heartbeat oscillation — us-west p95 spikes (Elmwood)

Thanks Olga — we saw timeouts in our user-facing summarization service around 08:52–09:00. One request id from our logs: req_20280301_085254_ab12.

A few questions:
1) Is the fallback to the model variant expected to change output characteristics? We need to know if there will be any semantic differences.
2) Can you confirm whether this qualifies under our SLA for service credits if errors exceed the p95 availability target for the hour?

Appreciate the quick update — we rely on consistent p95 behavior for our realtime workflows, so any timeline for full remediation would be helpful.

— Sarah
Sarah Jenner
Head of Platform Engineering, Elmwood Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.inference>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference>
Date: 2028-03-01T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Generation heartbeat oscillation — engineering notes and next steps

Folks — quick engineering summary for the thread (logs attached to internal trace):
- Root cause hypothesis: A kernel selection heuristic we enabled last week leads to oscillating kernel choices under a certain sequence length distribution, causing periodic KV cache pressure and extra context-switches on the us-west worker shard.
- What we changed: rolled back the kernel heuristic on the affected pool, enabled the model-variant fallback rule, and drained the shard for a rolling restart. Early telemetry after the rollback shows p95 returning to within expected baseline in the last 10 minutes.
- Action items:
  1) Collect and link all correlated traces for req_20280301_085254_ab12 — (action: Sean, ETA 60m).
  2) Run an automated A/B to verify output parity between primary and fallback model-variant for a representative prompt set (action: Marissa, ETA EOD today).
  3) Draft postmortem and a short customer-facing summary for Elmwood (action: Olga, ETA 48h).

Log snippets and a short diagnostic are saved to the incident folder; sharing the postmortem draft link to Elmwood once we have the parity check results.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
(attachment: internal_trace_usw_shard_17.log text/plain)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.inference>
To: Sarah Jenner <sarah.jenner@elmwoodhealth.com>
Cc: ops+elmwood@elmwoodhealth.com, marissa.cole@redwood.inference
Date: 2028-03-03T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Incident resolved — postmortem timeline and next steps (Elmwood)

Hi Sarah —

Following up: the immediate issue is resolved and p95 has stabilized in us-west. We completed the parity A/B for a 250-sample prompt set; differences between the primary model and the fallback variant were non-material for the Elmwood workload (summary attached in the postmortem draft).

Summary of next steps and commitments:
- Full postmortem (draft) attached for your review: postmortem-draft-elmwood.docx. We plan to publish a customer-facing summary on the status page by 2028-03-05 and will include the technical timeline and mitigations.
- SLA: we will run the standard availability calculation for the impacted window and share any applicable credit calculation by 2028-03-06. If you prefer a direct call to walk through the postmortem, I'm available tomorrow 10–12 PDT.
- Preventative work: engineering will remove the heuristic from all production pools until we ship a safer rollout strategy, and add a targeted canary + synthetic prompt set for early detection.

Apologies again for the disruption — thank you for the request id (that helped with trace correlation). If you have any questions on the draft or want us to redact anything before sharing broadly, say the word.

Best,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Account Lead, Customer Operations
Redwood Inference
